solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Boot produced in New Zealand city

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a rubber waterproof boot
second meaning: the capital of New Zealand

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests footwear made in a New Zealand factory; in fact the boot and the city simply share a name.
explanation.definitionFit: A wellington is a rubber knee boot, and Wellington is also the capital city of New Zealand.

clue.text: Small group in West Indies close to supply of drink

indicators.note: in tells us the small group goes inside the word for close

parts.note: close (nearby) means near
a cell is a small group, as in a terrorist or party cell

explanation.surface: A small band of people in the Caribbean living near the place where drink is kept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like it places the group inside the West Indies, but it actually works on the word for close that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine cellar is a stock of wine kept in a cellar, so it is a store of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Left, for instance? There's a right one, too!

definitions.text: Left, for instance? There's a right one, too!

parts.note: e.g. (exempli gratia) means for instance

explanation.surface: A puzzle about sides: if there is a left one, there must be a right one too.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: there is a left leg and a right leg. The wordplay is L for left plus EG for 'for instance'.
explanation.definitionFit: Limbs come in pairs, so a left lower limb has a matching right one, which is what the clue hints at.

clue.text: Narrow strip of land is accordingly crossing motorway

indicators.note: here the word for accordingly crosses, so it spans and contains the motorway letter

parts.note: thus means accordingly, therefore
M stands for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: A description of a slim spit of land with a motorway running across it.
explanation.definitionFit: An isthmus is a thin neck of land joining two larger landmasses, with water on both sides.

clue.text: Acquisitive editor printed in paler black?

indicators.note: printed in means the editor's letters are set inside the colour word, as type is set on a page

parts.note: grey is a paler shade of black

explanation.surface: A grasping newspaper editor appears in faded black ink.
explanation.definitionFit: Acquisitive means eager to gain possessions, which is what a greedy person always wants.

clue.text: Meat product not fresh? Not quite entirely

parts.note: food that is off has gone bad, not fresh

indicators.note: not quite means the word for entirely is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: all means entirely, wholly

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a meat product has gone bad, and the answer is: not completely.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal is the edible internal organs of an animal, such as liver and kidneys, sold as butchers' meat.

clue.text: Remarkable industrial action

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... as an adjective, eye-catching and notable
second meaning: ... as in workers going on strike

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like praise for a notable piece of industrial action, but the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Something striking attracts attention; workers striking are withdrawing their labour in a dispute.

clue.text: Dark period — imminent source of trouble

parts.note: nigh means near, close at hand, imminent

indicators.note: source of means the first letter of the next word, where it starts

explanation.surface: A warning that a dark time is coming, bringing trouble with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is the hours of darkness between sunset and sunrise, the daily dark period.

clue.text: Feeble leaders from England and France attending festivity

indicators.note: leaders means the first letters of the following words

parts.note: a fete is a festival or outdoor festivity

explanation.surface: Weak heads of government from England and France turn up at a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Effete describes someone weak, ineffectual and lacking vigour, so it is a close synonym of feeble.

clue.text: Resolved main fear about start of fine novel

indicators.note: resolved, read as re-solved, means worked out again, so the letters of main are rearranged
about means the fear word goes around the next letter

parts.note: alarm is a sudden fear

indicators.note: start of means the first letter of fine

explanation.surface: A main worry has been settled concerning the beginning of a good story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resolved' reads as settled, but split as re-solved it means worked out again, a rearrangement; fear gives ALARM, not a word to be shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Animal Farm is George Orwell's 1945 satirical fable about farm animals overthrowing their owner, a famous novel.

clue.text: Return of tailless bird provides something to chew over

indicators.note: return means the remaining letters are read backwards
tailless means the bird's last letter is cut off

parts.note: a duck is a bird

explanation.surface: A bird coming back without its tail gives someone food for thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailless' takes DUCK to DUC; 'Return of' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Cud is partly digested food that cows bring up and chew again, hence 'chew the cud'.

clue.text: Stated: "Last month Liberal will get ahead of a Communist"

parts.note: December is the last month of the year, abbreviated DEC
L is the abbreviation for Liberal in politics
a red is a communist

explanation.surface: A pundit predicts that last month the Liberals will lead a Communist in the polls.
explanation.definitionFit: To declare something is to announce or say it openly, so declared is a synonym of stated.

clue.text: Award no mild ale after brewing

indicators.note: brewing means the letters are stirred up and mixed, as beer is brewed

explanation.surface: A prize goes to a beer that is not a mild ale once it is brewed.
explanation.definitionFit: A medallion is a large medal, given as a prize or decoration.

clue.text: Insect not found to contain copper

indicators.note: to contain means the word for not found holds the copper symbol inside it

parts.note: something lost has not been found
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: An insect that cannot be found inside some copper.
explanation.definitionFit: A locust is a large grasshopper that swarms and destroys crops.

clue.text: School is beginning to mend division of opinion

indicators.note: beginning to means take the first letter of the word mend

explanation.surface: A school is starting to repair a rift among its staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A schism is a split within a group caused by disagreement, especially in a church.

clue.text: Fantastic castle turned up: item at auction

parts.note: to turn up is to arrive, so turned up means came
a lot is an item put up for sale at auction

explanation.surface: A fairytale castle appeared as an item at an auction sale.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turned up' looks like a reversal signal, but here it simply means arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: Camelot is King Arthur's legendary castle and court, a place of myth rather than history.

clue.text: Pay attention: there's something false about street name

indicators.note: about means the word for something false goes around the street letters

parts.note: a lie is something false

explanation.surface: A warning to take note: a street name has something fake about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To listen is to give heed and attend to what is being said.

clue.text: Chairman's upset, advocating disorder

definitions.note: a noun phrase sense: the doctrine of advocating disorder, i.e. the political creed against all government

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A company chairman is upset because someone is calling for chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchism is the political belief that all government should be abolished, which opponents call promoting lawlessness.

clue.text: It gives one pause, particularly in this clue

definitions.text: It gives one pause, particularly in this clue

parts.words: It gives one pause, particularly in this clue
parts.note: a punctuation mark marks a short pause in reading, and one appears in this very clue after 'pause'

explanation.walkthrough: 'gives one pause' sounds like making someone hesitate; the clue's own punctuation mark is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A comma is a punctuation mark showing a brief break in a sentence, and the clue contains one.

clue.text: Set goals every lesson, initially

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: A teacher sets learning goals at the start of every lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: To gel is to become firm or solidify, as a jelly sets.

clue.text: Allow recommendation regarding hairstyle?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... as a verb, to let something happen
second meaning, read as two words

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the answer as PERM IT, a hairdresser's advice; the question mark flags the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To permit is to give permission for something, so it is a synonym of allow.

clue.text: A lot of shops brought back source of wool

indicators.note: brought back means the letters are returned, read in reverse order

parts.note: a mall is a large collection of shops

explanation.surface: Someone has fetched wool back from a lot of shops.
explanation.definitionFit: A llama is a South American camelid kept for its soft fleece, which is spun into yarn.

clue.text: Took nutrition at end of race

indicators.note: end of means take the last letter of the word race

parts.note: the answer also appears across 'at end' in the clue, but that is a coincidence; the setter builds it from AT plus the last letter of race

explanation.surface: A runner had something to eat when the race was over.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat is to take in food, so ate is a past tense meaning consumed food.

clue.text: Normal electricity supply runs into working unit

parts.note: the mains is the household electricity supply

indicators.note: into means the runs letter goes inside the word for working unit

parts.note: a team is a unit of people working together
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Ordinary mains power flows into a work team's equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Mainstream means conventional, belonging to the ordinary majority view.
